chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said:

I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man had a canal in a town, and a man intended to dig another canal to his own town. What should be the distance between them so that one does not harm the other in the land, whether it is solid or soft? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'According to the reckoning that one of the two does not harm the other, if Allah wills.'

He said: And I wrote to him (peace be upon him): A man had a mill on the river of a town, and the town belonged to another man. So the owner of the town intended to divert the water to his town through a different river, thereby disabling this mill. Is that for him or not? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should fear Allah and act with goodness in that, and not harm his believing brother.'

key_terms.يُعَطِّلَ: To disable or put out of operation

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal conditions for diverting water or digging new canals without harming neighbors?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm and no causing harm) in the context of property rights, specifically regarding irrigation canals and water mills. It highlights that while ownership grants the right to utilize resources, this right is limited by the obligation to avoid detrimental impact on neighbors, reflecting the broader ethical mandate of 'al-ma'ruf' (good conduct) in social transactions.
